solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Heard private detective cry out for Magnum? (3,5)

indicators.note: what is heard is the sound, so the phrase is spoken and respelt

blocks.note: a private eye is a private detective; to scream is to cry out

annotation.surface: A gumshoe letting out a yell in the hope of summoning Magnum, the TV private investigator.
annotation.walkthrough: Magnum looks like the moustached TV detective, which suits the surface; it is really the brand of ice cream on a stick, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Magnum is a well-known brand of ice cream bar.

entries.clue: Forcefully demand where publicity should go to expose sadist (6)

indicators.note: the publicity, AD, is told to leave the word it sits in

blocks.note: in = where, as in the place something is

blocks.clueFragment: publicity should go to expose sadist
blocks.note: SADIST with AD, publicity, taken out

annotation.surface: A demand that the newspapers name and shame a cruel person.
annotation.walkthrough: AD is the usual crossword abbreviation for an advertisement, and so for publicity; removing it from SADIST leaves SIST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to insist is to demand something firmly.

entries.clue: Dropping cover, tearaways blunder (5)

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outer pair of letters, which are dropped

blocks.note: a little terror is a tearaway, an unruly child
TERRORS without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Reckless youngsters breaking cover and giving themselves away.
annotation.walkthrough: A tearaway is British for a wild, reckless young person, as is a terror.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a careless mistake.

entries.clue: Meet in Turin on base (3,4)

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupt, so the letters are corrupted into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Arranging a rendezvous at a base in the Italian city of Turin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meet in Turin' reads as a whole instruction, but 'in' belongs to nothing: the fodder is 'Turin on', and 'base' is an adjective of corruption, not a place.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to run into someone is to meet them by chance.

entries.clue: Article Cambridge’s lead historian possibly carbon dated wrongly (13)

indicators.note: the lead of Cambridge is its first letter
the letters are one possible arrangement of another

blocks.note: an indefinite article
first letter of Cambridge
anagram fodder
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

annotation.surface: A Cambridge historian's paper where the carbon dating has gone awry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carbon dated' pulls together as the dating technique, but carbon is only the letter C and 'dated wrongly' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something anachronistic is placed in the wrong period, dated wrongly.

entries.clue: Caught tenor playing musical instrument (6)

indicators.note: the letters of TENOR are played about with

blocks.note: c = caught, in cricket scoring
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A tenor singer caught in the act of playing an instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: The tenor looks like a musician in the scene, but he is only letters; C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: A cornet is a brass instrument like a small trumpet.

entries.clue: Indignation of Republican consumed by loss of power? (7)

indicators.note: R is swallowed up by the other word

blocks.note: a power outage is a cut in the electricity
R = Republican

annotation.surface: A Republican politician fuming after losing power at an election.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'loss of power' as political defeat; it is an electricity cut.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: outrage is angry indignation.

entries.clue: Innocent outing ruined — this’ll upset everybody, ultimately (3,6)

indicators.note: OUTING is wrecked and its letters rebuilt
take the final letter of each word

blocks.note: anagram fodder
last letters of this'll, upset and everybody

annotation.surface: An innocent day out spoiled, to the dismay of the whole party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like a second anagram signal, but it is just one of the three words giving a last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a verdict of not guilty declares someone innocent.

entries.clue: Believer in divine wisdom hopes to fake death at the end (8)

indicators.note: the letters of 'hopes to' are faked into a new word
only the final letter of death is wanted

blocks.note: anagram fodder
last letter of death

annotation.surface: Someone of faith planning to fake their own death.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To fake' reads as part of the plot; 'to' is fodder and 'fake' alone is the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A theosoph is a theosophist, who claims mystical knowledge of God; theosophy literally means divine wisdom.

entries.clue: Crafts turning north, back around port (9)

indicators.note: ARTS is turned to read backwards
REAR is brought round to read backwards

blocks.note: arts and crafts
N = north
the rear is the back

annotation.surface: Boats turning north and doubling back round a harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: Stranraer is a ferry port in south-west Scotland. 'Crafts' looks like boats but is skills, ARTS.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Stranraer is a Scottish port.

entries.clue: Means to hold up a bank? (9,4)

definitions.text: Means to hold up a bank?

blocks.note: on the surface, a way to rob at gunpoint; really a way to support something
on the surface a building full of money; really a sloping bank of earth

annotation.surface: A would-be robber asking how to stick up a bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hold up a bank' suggests an armed robbery; the bank is a slope of earth and holding it up means supporting it.
annotation.definitionFit: A retaining wall holds back a bank of earth, stopping it slumping.

entries.clue: Pupil that displeases me with low grades (5)

blocks.note: tut is what you say when something displeases you
two E grades, low marks

annotation.surface: A teacher complaining about a student who keeps getting poor marks.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'that displeases me' is what TUT says, an exclamation of annoyance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word for whoever a tutor teaches.

entries.clue: Crush Charlie and speed inside school (7)

indicators.note: 'Charlie and speed inside school' puts those two pieces physically within the school's letters

blocks.note: sch is an abbreviation for school
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
to run is to speed along

annotation.surface: A schoolyard crush on a boy called Charlie, plus some illicit speed.
annotation.walkthrough: Crush and Charlie suggest a romance, and Charlie and speed both hint at drugs; all three are misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to scrunch something is to crush it up.

entries.clue: Parts of service briefly show successful periods (7)

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: TEACH, to show how, without its last letter
ups, as in ups and downs

annotation.surface: A church or army service summarised in a few highlights.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests worship or duty; here it is a tea service, a matching set of crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tea service is a matching crockery set, and the cups are among its pieces.

entries.clue: One facilitating temporary connections in current affairs? (9,4)

definitions.text: One facilitating temporary connections in current affairs?

blocks.note: on the surface a networker making introductions; really a spring clip that joins wires for a moment
on the surface the news; really matters of electric current

annotation.surface: A news fixer who briefly introduces people in the world of topical events.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current affairs' means the news, but the current is electric: this clip makes temporary connections in circuits.
annotation.definitionFit: A crocodile clip joins wires temporarily in an electrical circuit.

entries.clue: Brown bird eating nuts thrown over fence at the back (9)

indicators.note: the bird swallows the nuts
LOCO is flipped to read backwards
only the last letter of fence is used

blocks.note: a chat is a small songbird
loco = crazy, nuts
last letter of fence

annotation.surface: A brown bird pecking at nuts tossed over the back fence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brown bird' pairs naturally, but Brown is the definition and the bird is separate.
annotation.definitionFit: A colour name taken from the food: the deep shade of a bar of dark chocolate.

entries.clue: One’s positive Tim’s wearing cycling top (8)

definitions.note: reads as 'one who is positive', a noun phrase

indicators.note: TIM IS is worn inside the top
TOP cycles its letters, moving the T from front to back

blocks.note: TOP with its first letter moved to the end
Tim's expanded as Tim is

annotation.surface: A cheerful man called Tim sporting a cycling jersey.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Tim's stands for 'is', not possession, so it gives TIM IS. A cycling top sounds like a jersey; here it tells you to rotate TOP.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the person who looks on the bright side, expecting things to turn out well.

entries.clue: Following pressure, virile boy hit out in a forbidding way? (13)

indicators.note: the anagram comes after P
the letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: p = pressure
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A macho lad lashing out after being put under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts P first: the rearranged letters follow the pressure.
annotation.definitionFit: Prohibitively means so as to forbid or prevent, in a forbidding way.

entries.clue: Setter strove to get hold of gold supplied with teeth (7)

indicators.note: VIED gets hold of OR, holding it inside

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I
vied = competed, strove
or is gold in heraldry

annotation.surface: The crossword setter's struggle to win gold, perhaps in a gold-toothed grin.
annotation.walkthrough: Ivories is slang for teeth, so ivoried means given teeth.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: ivories are teeth, so the adjective describes a mouth given a set of them.

entries.clue: Draws forth a lot of criticism about supporting priest (7)

indicators.note: most of STICK, losing its last letter
the letters are turned about to read backwards
in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath ELI

blocks.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
STICK, criticism, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A priest attracting a barrage of criticism.
annotation.walkthrough: To get stick is British slang for being criticised. ELI is the crossword's favourite priest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to elicit a response is to draw it forth.

entries.clue: Fashionable model joins university, occupying appropriate position (2,4)

indicators.note: to join something is to attach yourself to it, so the model's letters sit right next to the university's

blocks.note: in = fashionable
to sit for a painter is to model
U = university

annotation.surface: A fashion model enrolling at a university.
annotation.walkthrough: Model looks like a noun, a catwalk figure; it is the verb sit, as for a portrait.
annotation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original or proper place.

entries.clue: Press dismissed resolve (4,3)

blocks.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

annotation.surface: Reporters sent away showing determination.
annotation.walkthrough: Press looks like the newspapers and resolve like determination; both are verbs here.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: smoothing away a difficulty as you smooth creases from cloth.

entries.clue: Dog wearing smile, not inclined toward being recalled (7)

indicators.note: the grin is worn around the other piece
OFF is called back, so it reads in reverse

blocks.note: a grin is a broad smile
off, as in off your food

annotation.surface: A grinning dog that refuses to come back when called.
annotation.walkthrough: Being off something means having lost the taste for it, so not inclined toward it.
annotation.definitionFit: A griffon is a breed of small wiry-coated dog.

entries.clue: Stupid criticism — end of story (5)

indicators.note: only the last letter of story is taken

blocks.note: flak is strong criticism
last letter of story

annotation.surface: Someone dismissing a silly objection with 'end of story'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of story' is a set phrase meaning no more discussion; here it just gives Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Flaky is informal for scatty or unreliable, loosely stupid.

entries.clue: Heads off idle remarks about quotes in Arabic dialect (5)

indicators.note: the heads, the first letters, are taken off the following words

blocks.note: first letters of idle, remarks, about, quotes, in

annotation.surface: Someone cutting short the chatter about quotations in Arabic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' sounds like forestalling; it means take the heads of the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the regional varieties of spoken Arabic, named after its country.

entries.clue: Din, daily one, semi-uncertain (9)

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the word is used

blocks.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady who comes in daily
I = one
the first half of VARIABLE, uncertain

annotation.surface: Noise from a daily newspaper that cannot quite make up its mind.
annotation.walkthrough: A daily looks like a newspaper; in British usage it is also a cleaner, as is a char.
annotation.definitionFit: A charivari is a cacophony, originally a mock serenade with pots and pans.

entries.clue: Attempt to keep close in (6)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so the attempt holds the close within its letters

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
the close is the end

annotation.surface: An effort to stay indoors.
annotation.walkthrough: The one-word definition 'in' is easy to overlook: it means fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: In and trendy both mean fashionable.

entries.clue: British, with the exception of Times readers, comment on expulsion? (5,3)

blocks.note: B = British
less = minus, except
the solvers reading this paper are you

annotation.surface: A remark on a Brexit-style expulsion that exempts subscribers to the Times.
annotation.walkthrough: Expulsion sounds like being thrown out; it is the air expelled in a sneeze, which is greeted with 'bless you'.
annotation.definitionFit: Bless you is what people say after a sneeze, a violent expulsion of air.
